subject.title: fix(gateway): reject disallowed browser Origin before accepting auth.mode=none on HTTP (#102834)

question: Should this PR's HTTP browser-Origin gate apply broadly before token/password auth as well as before auth.mode none, or should it be narrowed to the no-auth gap only?
rationale: The fix closes a real Gateway auth/CSRF gap, but it changes a security-sensitive compatibility boundary for Origin-bearing HTTP clients and the linked issue is already marked for maintainer security/product review.

options.title: Approve Broad HTTP Origin Gate
options.body: Accept the shared gate for any Origin-bearing HTTP request, require live after-fix proof, and call out the compatibility behavior in release context.

options.title: Narrow To None Mode
options.body: Move the new check so token/password HTTP clients retain current behavior, and add regression coverage for both none-mode and shared-secret cases.

options.title: Hold For Policy Decision
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers decide explicit no-auth HTTP should remain pure no-auth and only be documented as unsafe for browser exposure.

recommendation.title: Approve Broad HTTP Origin Gate
recommendation.body: Accept the shared gate for any Origin-bearing HTTP request, require live after-fix proof, and call out the compatibility behavior in release context.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across Gateway Origin, auth hardening, and the security-boundary decisions this PR changes.
